threat: Code in an Actor escapes its sandbox to the worker pod or node.
mitigating_invariants: Every Actor runs in its own gVisor sandbox or micro-VM; capabilities can only be changed within validated bounds; images are digest-pinned.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Track gVisor and Cloud Hypervisor security releases through SandboxConfig versions; run workers on dedicated, tainted nodes; keep `--cordon-system-infra-components` on.
notes: The isolation strength comes from the chosen backend; the micro-VM class adds a hardware boundary.

threat: An Actor reaches another Actor on the same worker over the network.
mitigating_invariants: Each Actor has its own network namespace; its egress only leaves through the tunnel to the egress gateway; the router reaches Actors only through the worker tunnel with mTLS.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add an e2e check that two Actors on one worker cannot connect to each other's addresses.
notes: Depends on the tunnel running in worker pods; see the README status section.

threat: An Actor reaches the keeper, the worker's Unix sockets or other node-local services.
mitigating_invariants: The sandbox mount set is built only from the template's declared volumes and fixed system mounts; sockets that carry Actor credentials (keeper dial from the worker and tunnel) are mutually authenticated with pod certificates and same-node checks.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Periodically audit the sandbox mount set produced by the OCI spec builders in `hivekeep-imagecache::ocispec`.

threat: An Actor reads or overwrites another Actor's snapshots.
mitigating_invariants: Snapshot objects sit under `hives/<hive>/actors/<uid>`; for GCS, node credentials are downscoped per Actor (read-write own prefix, read-only completed Tags) and issued only for Actors bound to the calling node.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add per-Actor scoping for the S3 backend, which currently uses the plugin's ambient credentials.

threat: A tampered or corrupt snapshot is restored into an Actor.
mitigating_invariants: Snapshot manifests are written last as commit markers; the sparse format reader validates its framing; restore needs a compatible runtime stamp.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add content digests or a MAC over snapshot manifests and verify them on restore.
notes: Integrity against a party with bucket write access currently relies on bucket access control.

threat: An Actor uses its egress to reach cloud metadata, the Kubernetes API or internal Services.
mitigating_invariants: Egress is deny-by-default per Actor; UDP is always blocked; destinations must match a hostname-pattern rule and port; addresses match only `*`; DNS answers are filtered by the same policy.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Document a recommended deny list for `*` rules; alert on policies containing `*` with all ports.

threat: A credential the Actor's traffic needs leaks from the sandbox (for example, through prompt injection).
mitigating_invariants: Injected credentials never enter the sandbox: the Actor sends a placeholder and the egress gateway replaces the header for matching rules only.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Prefer `actor_jwt` injection with short expirations over static secrets where the upstream accepts JWTs.
notes: Credentials the template itself puts in env vars or files are not protected by this.

threat: An Actor obtains identity credentials for a different Actor.
mitigating_invariants: Actor certificates and JWTs are minted only by the control plane: through Control for the egress gateway role, or through WorkerService for a keeper on the Actor's current node.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add a regression e2e test that minting for an Actor on another node returns NOT_FOUND.

threat: An Actor that keeps getting resumed on new Workers uses the moves to spread laterally.
mitigating_invariants: A restore starts a fresh sandbox; a restarted worker's previous Actors are crashed by epoch fencing; RUNNING commits are fenced on the placement epoch.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Rate-limit `RequestActorSuspend` from workers per Actor.

threat: A malicious image or workload exhausts node CPU, memory, disk or file descriptors.
mitigating_invariants: CPU and memory limits are enforced per Actor through cgroup leaves; the scheduler books limits plus runtime overhead; the image cache evicts at high and low watermarks.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add per-Actor disk quotas for durable-dir and rootfs layers; limit image size at pull time.
notes: The glutton workload in `hivekeep-bench` exercises these limits.

threat: An Actor learns cluster topology from what it can see inside the sandbox.
mitigating_invariants: The sandbox gets a generated `resolv.conf` and `hosts`; system-info volumes expose only the Actor's own name, Hive, UID and allow-listed trust bundles.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Review the guest-visible environment for each sandbox class before 1.0.

threat: A caller in one Hive reads or changes resources in another Hive.
mitigating_invariants: Every Control RPC derives its authorization check from validated identifiers before running; Hive roles are evaluated against that Hive's policy only; the store rejects cross-hive references.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Keep the authz e2e suite (`crates/hivekeep-e2e/tests/authz/`) in the release gate.

threat: Anyone on the internal network calls `hivekeep-api` or the keeper without credentials.
mitigating_invariants: `hivekeep-api` requires a trusted JWT or a client certificate on every call; the keeper accepts only the control plane's SPIFFE ID; NetworkPolicies limit who can reach system pods.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Refuse to start `hivekeep-api` without `--grpc-server-cred-bundle` unless an explicit development flag is set.

threat: A template author abuses template fields to escalate (for example by adding capabilities, picking a storage location or mounting host paths).
mitigating_invariants: Templates are validated field by field; capabilities are bounded; `storage_location` is honored only with the `PerTemplateSnapshotLocation` preview gate; volume sources are limited to durable-dir, image, system-info and CSI external volumes.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Restrict template creation to Hive editors (the default) and review editors regularly.

threat: A shared bootstrap owner grants every holder of its token global ownership.
mitigating_invariants: Bootstrap owners must be configured explicitly; the installer warns when the shared `hivekeep-client` ServiceAccount is one.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Set `--api-authz-bootstrap-owners` to operator principals and manage the rest through access policies.

threat: A flood of requests or Actors exhausts the API, the router or cluster capacity.
mitigating_invariants: Resume requests share one flight per Actor; the parking lot has a fixed capacity and sheds with 503; per-pool capacity bounds placement.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add per-principal rate limits on Control and per-Hive Actor quotas.

threat: An egress policy grants more than intended through broad patterns.
mitigating_invariants: Patterns are exact, `*.suffix` or `*`; the most specific match wins; rules that fail to compile are dropped (narrowing only); at most 256 rules.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Provide a dry-run evaluator in `hivectl` that shows which rule would decide a destination.

threat: A compromised keeper reads snapshots of Actors that are not on its node.
mitigating_invariants: WorkerService answers NOT_FOUND for Workers and Actors on other nodes; the credential exchange binds issuance to the Actor's current node.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Shorten the lifetime of downscoped tokens and alert on exchange refusals.

threat: A compromised node escalates to the control plane or other nodes.
mitigating_invariants: Keepers authenticate as their DaemonSet ServiceAccount; the control plane checks pod UID and node when dialing keepers; keeper roles are limited to node-scoped WorkerService calls and egress policy reads.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Bind the keeper ServiceAccount's Kubernetes RBAC to read-only, node-scoped access.

threat: A compromised gate component misuses its control-plane role.
mitigating_invariants: The egress gateway's role is limited to reading Actors and egress policies and minting Actor credentials; the router's role is limited to listing and resuming Actors.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Run the egress gateway's ext_proc without Kubernetes access (the egress mode already needs none).

threat: Signing keys (CA pools, JWT pool) are stolen from Secrets.
mitigating_invariants: Pools live in Secrets in `hivekeep-system`; JWT keys rotate through add, activate and remove; leaf certificates are short-lived.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Store pools in an external KMS-backed signer; restrict Secret access in `hivekeep-system` to the components that mount them.

threat: Traffic between components is intercepted or spoofed.
mitigating_invariants: Component traffic uses mTLS with pinned SPIFFE IDs or Service DNS names; the router verifies the worker's SPIFFE ID recorded on the assignment.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Enable dual-stack NetworkPolicies alongside mTLS.

threat: A stale egress policy keeps applying after it changes.
mitigating_invariants: The gateway caches policies for at most `--egress-policy-cache-ttl` (10s by default); the tunnel's policy source is a short-lived, deduplicated cache.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Push policy invalidations from the control plane instead of relying on the TTL.

threat: Insiders with database or bucket access read Actor state.
mitigating_invariants: Database roles are split between owner and read-write; bundled PostgreSQL uses certificate logins; snapshot paths are owner-scoped.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Encrypt snapshots with per-Actor keys before upload.

threat: Malicious activity goes unrecorded or unnoticed.
mitigating_invariants: The control plane records Actor state changes, crashes and deletes with attribution; worker logs carry Actor, Hive and template labels; Prometheus metrics cover lifecycle errors and crashes.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Wire `hivekeep-telemetry` into the service binaries for OTLP export, and ship an alerting rule set.

threat: A detected malicious Actor cannot be contained quickly.
mitigating_invariants: Deleting the EgressPolicy removes all egress; suspend, revert and delete work from any state; Workers can be drained.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Add a single "quarantine" verb that strips egress and suspends.

threat: Production installs keep development placeholders (domain, OID arc, trust domain).
mitigating_invariants: Every such value is listed in `PLACEHOLDERS.md`.
suggested_concrete_mitigations: Fail the release image build when placeholder values remain.
